gaps: CRITICAL - Pointer Lock in the Mac app: element.requestPointerLock() is refused in Tauri v2 WKWebView (wry issue 445, open since 2021, last comment 2026-08-25). A native cursor grab (notes 2, option A) must be built and tested on macOS 15, 26 and 27. I could not runtime-test requestPointerLock in a headless WKWebView because it needs a user gesture; the conclusion comes from WebKit and wry source plus two shipping Tauri apps that work around it.

Option A cursor grab gives OS-accelerated deltas (no unadjustedMovement equivalent). Raw input in the Mac app would need option B (private WebKit delegate) or a native event tap. Decide after playtesting.

Option B uses a private WebKit selector (_webViewDidRequestPointerLock:completionHandler:). Fine for a notarized direct download, likely rejected by the Mac App Store, and it can break on an OS update.

WKWebView caps requestAnimationFrame at 60 fps on macOS 13-15 (ProMotion displays included); the cap is gone on macOS 26+. tauri-plugin-macos-fps 0.1.0 lifts it through a private preference. Fallback: accept 60 fps on older macOS.

No verified CC0 outdoor impulse response with a login-free direct URL. OpenAIR is per-item Creative Commons (mostly CC BY 4.0, some stricter), Freesound CC0 IRs need a login to download, EchoThief forbids game use without a licence. Fallback: generate IRs procedurally at load time (notes 5). Second fallback outside the licence rule: Voxengo IM Reverbs (custom royalty-free licence, commercial use allowed), https://www.voxengo.com/files/impulses/IMreverbs.zip (7.07 MB, 206 OK) and single files such as https://oramics.github.io/sampled/IR/Voxengo/samples/parking_garage.wav (657,496 bytes, 206 OK).

macOS 26+ shows the Local Network permission prompt when RTCPeerConnection gathers mDNS host candidates (w3c/webrtc-pc issue 3109, open). Add NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription to Info.plist and keep STUN and TURN candidates so a denial does not break internet play. Same-LAN play after a denial is untested.

The free PeerJS cloud (0.peerjs.com) answered in 162 ms today but has no SLA and an open issue (#1350, Oct 2025) about 6+ minute WebSocket delays. Fallback and recommendation: own Cloudflare Worker + Durable Object signaling.
postprocessing 6.39.6 declares three < 0.188.0. Pin three to ~0.187.0 until postprocessing widens the range.

Tauri CSP for KTX2Loader is unverified in a real build: the loader starts workers from a blob: URL and compiles wasm, so the CSP most likely needs worker-src blob: and script-src 'wasm-unsafe-eval'. Fallback: leave app.security.csp null during development and tighten later.
unadjustedMovement on a Mac trackpad removes pointer acceleration and may feel slow; nobody documents the feel. Ship a raw-input toggle and test on a MacBook trackpad in Chrome and Safari.
Force click (webkitmouseforcedown and MouseEvent.webkitForce) is Safari-only per MDN data and untested in WKWebView. Treat it as an optional extra, never the only way to aim.

The share of players who need TURN (symmetric NAT, CGNAT, campus networks) is an estimate (often quoted 10-20 percent). Fallback: always include Cloudflare TURN credentials; 2-player traffic stays far below the 1,000 GB free tier.
HRTF voice budget (6-8 simultaneous HRTF panners) is an estimate, not a measurement. Fallback: switch distant voices to equalpower and measure on an Intel MacBook Air class machine.
gltf-transform uastc/etc1s flag spellings beyond --slots were read from source option names, not from a run. Check gltf-transform uastc --help before scripting the asset pipeline.

- postprocessing 6.39.6 (2026-11-01). peerDependency three '>= 0.168.0 < 0.188.0', so r187 is supported. Stay on 6.x (7.0.0-beta.16 exists).
- n8ao 2.0.1. peers: postprocessing >=6.30.0, three >=0.137.
- three-mesh-bvh 0.9.18. peer three >=0.159.0.
- @tauri-apps/cli 2.12.4 and @tauri-apps/api 2.12.4; Rust crates tauri 2.12.5, wry 0.57.1, tao 0.37.2.
- vite 8.3.7, needs Node ^20.19.0 or >=22.12.0.
- Also checked: peerjs 1.5.5 (last publish 2025-06), trystero 0.26.0, @gltf-transform/cli 4.5.1 (Node >=20), meshoptimizer 1.3.0, KTX-Software 4.4.2, @dimforge/rapier3d-compat 0.21.0, stats-gl 4.2.3, lil-gui 0.21.0. Skip realism-effects (last release 2023) and the three-csm package (2023); use three/addons/csm/CSM.js.
- N8AO inside the pmndrs composer (n8ao README): const composer = new EffectComposer(renderer, { frameBufferType: HalfFloatType }); composer.addPass(new RenderPass(scene, camera)); const ao = new N8AOPostPass(scene, camera, w, h); composer.addPass(ao); composer.addPass(new EffectPass(camera, new SMAAEffect({ preset: SMAAPreset.HIGH }), new ToneMappingEffect({ mode: ToneMappingMode.AGX }))). N8AOPostPass needs a RenderPass before it (N8AOPass replaces the render pass). ao.configuration.halfRes = true is a 2-4x speedup; ao.setQualityMode('Low' | 'Medium' | 'High' | 'Ultra'). gammaCorrection is auto-set from the pass position; set ao.configuration.gammaCorrection = false if colours look washed out. The README says hardware MSAA does not work with the AO and recommends SMAA.
- Renderer setup per the postprocessing README: new WebGLRenderer({ powerPreference: 'high-performance', antialias: false, stencil: false, depth: false }), renderer.toneMapping = NoToneMapping, tone map with ToneMappingEffect as the last effect.
Sources: https://registry.npmjs.org/postprocessing , https://github.com/N8python/n8ao#readme , https://github.com/pmndrs/postprocessing#readme

2. POINTER LOCK IN TAURI V2 ON MACOS (WKWebView)
- It does not work out of the box. WebKit's UIDelegate.mm answers requestPointerLock with false unless the embedder's WKUIDelegate implements the private method _webViewDidRequestPointerLock:completionHandler:. wry 0.57.1's delegate implements only windowWillClose, runOpenPanel and requestMediaCapturePermission. The page sees a rejected request.
- Tauri 2.12.0 exposed wry's permission handler with PermissionKind::PointerLock, but wry's own docs say PointerLock is supported on Linux only ('Windows / macOS / Android / iOS: Not yet supported by platform backends'). Do not rely on it.
- No Tauri pointer-lock plugin exists on crates.io or npm (searched today). Windows WebView2 grants pointer lock natively.
- Option A, recommended (public APIs only), as used by hew3d/hew (AGPL, read for the technique, do not copy code): a Rust command that (1) warps the cursor to the canvas centre with CGWarpMouseCursorPosition in screen coordinates, (2) calls window.set_cursor_grab(true), which in tao is CGAssociateMouseAndMouseCursorPosition(false) and freezes the cursor, (3) hides it with NSCursor hide. The webview keeps receiving mousemove with movementX/movementY because WebKit fills them from NSEvent deltaX/deltaY (WebEventFactory.mm), which keep flowing while the cursor is frozen. Unlock on Escape (handled in game code), on window blur and on window destroy; keep the hide/unhide calls balanced. A JS-only first attempt is possible: getCurrentWindow().setCursorGrab(true) and setCursorVisible(false) with capabilities core:window:allow-set-cursor-grab and core:window:allow-set-cursor-visible; move to the custom command if the cursor freezes off-canvas.
- Side benefits of option A: no browser 'press Esc' banner and no 1.25 s Chrome re-lock cooldown. Cost: deltas are OS-accelerated.
- Option B (real Pointer Lock, private API), as used by MiguelMedeiros/ghostly (MIT): class_addMethod the selector _webViewDidRequestPointerLock:completionHandler: onto wry's delegate class with type encoding 'v@:@@?', answer the block with YES, then set the webview's UIDelegate again because WebKit caches which methods exist. This gives pointerlockchange events and Safari's unadjustedMovement.
- Code shape: one PointerGrab interface with a web backend (requestPointerLock) and a tauri-macos backend (invoke), both feeding the same movementX/Y handler.
- Related Mac app facts: Tauri 2.12 no longer needs macos-private-api for fullscreen, and wry 0.56 enabled element fullscreen on macOS 12.3+. rAF is capped at 60 fps on macOS 13-15 and uncapped on macOS 26+.
Sources: https://github.com/tauri-apps/wry/issues/445 , https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/main/Source/WebKit/UIProcess/Cocoa/UIDelegate.mm , https://github.com/tauri-apps/wry/blob/dev/src/permissions.rs , https://github.com/tauri-apps/wry/blob/dev/src/wkwebview/class/wry_web_view_ui_delegate.rs , https://github.com/tauri-apps/tao/blob/dev/src/platform_impl/macos/window.rs , https://github.com/hew3d/hew/blob/main/shells/tauri/src-tauri/src/fly_cursor.rs , https://github.com/MiguelMedeiros/ghostly/blob/main/apps/desktop/src/app_sandbox.rs , https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/issues/13978 , https://docs.rs/tauri-plugin-macos-fps

3. TRACKPAD ERGONOMICS IN THE BROWSER
- Pointer lock movementX/Y works with a trackpad in Chrome, Safari and Firefox. unadjustedMovement (no OS acceleration): Chrome 88+ (macOS 10.15.1+), Safari 18.4+, Firefox 152+ (MDN compat data 8.1.8). Call await el.requestPointerLock({ unadjustedMovement: true }) in try/catch and retry without options. Safari before 18.4 and Chrome before 92 return undefined instead of a promise.
- Chrome refuses to re-lock for 1.25 s after the user presses Esc (SecurityError 'The user has exited the lock before this request was completed'). Show the pause menu, catch the rejection and retry on the next click. No cooldown when the page itself calls document.exitPointerLock().
- Chrome has a long-standing bug with occasional huge movementX/Y spikes; drop single-event outliers.
- navigator.keyboard.lock (capturing Esc) is Chrome-only and needs fullscreen; it is absent in Safari and WKWebView (confirmed by the local probe).
- Weapon switch on two-finger scroll: a trackpad sends a stream of small pixel deltas plus a momentum tail after the fingers lift, and the browser cannot tell the tail apart (Chromium issue 40704952). Accumulate deltaY, fire one switch when the sum passes about 50 px, then ignore wheel input until 150-200 ms pass with no wheel event. A notched mouse wheel sends about 100-120 per notch: one switch per notch. Register with { passive: false } and call preventDefault. Pinch arrives as wheel with ctrlKey true (Chrome, Firefox, Safari 15+): ignore it. Natural scrolling flips the sign, so offer an invert option.
- Always bind number keys 1-7 to the seven guns; that is the reliable path on a trackpad.
- Clicking: a physical click with the thumb while another finger moves works; tap-to-click cannot be held; a two-finger secondary click cannot be held while aiming. So aim-down-sights needs a keyboard path: right mouse button plus a hold key and a toggle option. Offer a fire key as well as left click.
- Use event.code, not event.key (Option changes characters on Mac). Ctrl+click is a context click on macOS: preventDefault the contextmenu event. While Cmd is held macOS swallows keyup for other keys, so never bind Cmd and clear all key state on blur and visibilitychange.
- Force click events (webkitmouseforcedown, webkitmouseforcechanged, MouseEvent.webkitForce) exist in Safari 9+ only, not Chrome.
Sources: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/requestPointerLock , https://issues.chromium.org/issues/40148473 , https://csarko.sh/research/pointer-lock-escape-cooldown , https://issues.chromium.org/issues/41404618 , https://issues.chromium.org/issues/40704952 , https://danburzo.ro/dom-gestures , https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=218054

4. RENDERING: REALISTIC AND EFFICIENT IN THREE r187
- Migration facts that affect new code: RGBELoader is now HDRLoader (r180); PCFSoftShadowMap is deprecated, PCFShadowMap is soft (r182); Clock is deprecated in favour of Timer (r183); PBR energy conservation and indirect specular changed (r181); PMREM was rewritten on cube render targets in r187, so old screenshots will not match.
- Shadows: three/addons/csm/CSM.js works with WebGLRenderer (CSMShadowNode is the WebGPU one). new CSM({ parent: scene, camera, cascades: 3, maxFar: 120, mode: 'practical', shadowMapSize: 2048, lightDirection }), then csm.setupMaterial(m) for every lit material (including GLTF ones) and csm.update() each frame. Each cascade renders the scene again, so tiers: high = 3 cascades at 2048; medium = 2 at 1024; low = one directional shadow map fitted to the map with renderer.shadowMap.autoUpdate = false (the sun never moves) plus blob shadows under characters. The maps are small, so maxFar of 100-150 m is enough.
- Environment: load a 1k or 2k .hdr with HDRLoader, run PMREMGenerator.fromEquirectangular, set scene.environment, dispose the generator. Use a separate 4k-8k JPG or KTX2 sky dome for the visible background; a 2k HDR is plenty for lighting.
- Tone mapping: AgX for golden hour and dusk (bright saturated light rolls off without hue shifts); Khronos Neutral keeps base colours truer but clips sooner; ACES Filmic adds contrast and shifts hues. postprocessing ToneMappingMode has AGX, NEUTRAL and ACES_FILMIC. Use HalfFloatType composer buffers (half-float render targets are available in WKWebView, local probe).
- Anti-aliasing: with a composer the canvas antialias flag does nothing. SMAAEffect (HIGH) is the default because N8AO does not work with MSAA; FXAAEffect on the low tier; EffectComposer({ multisampling: 4 }) only on a tier with AO off (MAX_SAMPLES is 8 on Apple GPUs).
- Dynamic resolution: Retina at 2x is four times the pixels and the largest single cost. Cap pixel ratio at min(devicePixelRatio, 1.5) on high and 1.0 on low. Keep a moving average of frame time and step renderer.setPixelRatio between 0.6x and 1.0x of the cap, then composer.setSize, at most once a second.
- Instancing: InstancedMesh for pines, grass cards, rocks, crates and containers; BatchedMesh (in core) for many different static meshes sharing one material. Culling is per InstancedMesh, so split instances by map cell. Foliage: alphaTest cut-outs, no blending. Use three-mesh-bvh (computeBoundsTree, acceleratedRaycast, firstHitOnly) for bullets, bot line of sight and player collision.
- KTX2: new KTX2Loader().setTranscoderPath('/basis/').detectSupport(renderer); gltfLoader.setKTX2Loader(ktx2).setMeshoptDecoder(MeshoptDecoder). Copy basis_transcoder.js and .wasm into public/basis/. WKWebView on Apple GPU reports ASTC, BPTC, S3TC and ETC2, so textures stay compressed in VRAM (4-8x less than RGBA8).
- Encoding: @gltf-transform/cli 4.5.1 shells out to the ktx binary (KTX-Software >= 4.4.0, 'ktx create'), not the old toktx. One step: gltf-transform optimize in.glb out.glb --texture-compress ktx2 --compress meshopt. Finer: gltf-transform uastc in.glb tmp.glb --slots '{normalTexture,occlusionTexture,metallicRoughnessTexture}' then gltf-transform etc1s tmp.glb out.glb for colour maps, then gltf-transform meshopt. Standalone textures, using the flags gltf-transform passes: ktx create --format R8G8B8A8_SRGB --assign-tf srgb --generate-mipmap --encode basis-lz --qlevel 128 --clevel 1 in.png out.ktx2 (colour) and ktx create --format R8G8B8A8_UNORM --assign-tf linear --generate-mipmap --encode uastc --uastc-quality 2 --zstd 18 in.png out.ktx2 (normal and ORM maps). ETC1S is smallest but damages normal maps; UASTC is near BC7 quality and larger.
- Meshopt over Draco: 29 KB decoder versus a 192 KB wasm, faster decode, and it also compresses animation.
Sources: https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/wiki/Migration-Guide , https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/r187/examples/jsm/csm/CSM.js , https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/r187/examples/webgl_shadowmap_csm.html , https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/r187/examples/jsm/loaders/KTX2Loader.js , https://github.com/pmndrs/postprocessing/blob/main/src/enums/ToneMappingMode.js , https://github.com/donmccurdy/glTF-Transform/blob/main/packages/cli/src/transforms/toktx.ts , https://github.com/KhronosGroup/KTX-Software/releases/tag/v4.4.2

5. WEB AUDIO REALISM
- HRTF cost: the spec calls equalpower 'simple and efficient'; Paul Adenot's Web Audio performance notes call an HRTF PannerNode 'very expensive' (continuous convolution, up to four convolvers for a moving stereo source, plus HRTF database memory) and equalpower 'rather cheap'. Chrome loads HRTF asynchronously, so the first HRTF sound can be late (web-audio-api issue 2449). Plan: HRTF for the 6-8 most important voices (enemy shots and footsteps), equalpower for the rest, plain stereo for the player's own gun. Feed mono buffers. Create one HRTF panner behind the loading screen to warm it up.
- Reverb: one ConvolverNode per map on a shared send bus, never one per sound. Generate the stereo impulse response in code: white noise times exp(-6.91 * t / RT60), with a lowpass that closes over time and two or three early taps, rendered once through an OfflineAudioContext. Starting points: Harbor RT60 0.9 s, bright, with a 60-90 ms slap off the walls; Pinewood 0.6 s, heavily damped highs, low wet level; Railyard 1.8 s, with a discrete echo at 150-250 ms. This removes the licence question.
- IR licences: OpenAIR is not CC0; each entry carries its own Creative Commons licence (most CC BY 4.0, check the page). EchoThief excludes games. Voxengo IM Reverbs has a custom royalty-free licence. Freesound user djericmark publishes CC0 alley, underpass and parking-garage IRs (pack 40453) but Freesound needs a login to download.
- Distance: PannerNode with distanceModel 'inverse', refDistance 3-5 m for gunshots. Add a BiquadFilterNode lowpass per voice with cutoff falling by distance, for example 18000 * 2^(-d / 50) Hz, floor 1500 Hz. Crossfade a close sample and a distant sample of each gun by distance; that sells range better than a filter alone. Occlusion: one BVH ray from listener to source; if blocked, cutoff about 1000 Hz and -6 to -9 dB.
- Speed of sound: delay = distance / 343 s (150 m is 0.44 s). Schedule with source.start(ctx.currentTime + d / 343); it is sample accurate and cheaper than a DelayNode. Muzzle flash and tracers stay instant. For rifle rounds play a short crack as the bullet passes the listener, then the report later. Doppler was removed from the spec.
- Housekeeping: resume the AudioContext on the click that grabs the pointer; latencyHint 'interactive'; a DynamicsCompressorNode as master limiter; decode everything to AudioBuffers (Safari has delay bugs with media-element sources, WebKit bug 221334).
Sources: https://webaudio.github.io/web-audio-api/#enumdef-panningmodeltype , https://padenot.github.io/web-audio-perf/ , https://github.com/WebAudio/web-audio-api/issues/2449 , https://openairlib.net/?page_id=2 , https://www.voxengo.com/impulses/ , https://freesound.org/people/djericmark/packs/40453/

6. P2P FOR TWO PLAYERS (BROWSER AND TAURI)
- Transport: one RTCPeerConnection with two data channels: 'state' { ordered: false, maxRetransmits: 0 } for 20-30 Hz snapshots and inputs, 'events' (reliable, ordered) for hits, kills and round state. The host simulates bots and validates hits.
- WebRTC in Tauri WKWebView: works. Local probe on macOS 27.2: typeof RTCPeerConnection is 'function' and createDataChannel plus createOffer produce a webrtc-datachannel SDP. Data-only connections need no camera or microphone permission. If the app is sandboxed it needs com.apple.security.network.client (tauri-docs issue 3171). The production origin is tauri://localhost, so the signaling Worker must accept that Origin.
- macOS 26+ shows the Local Network prompt when a peer connection gathers mDNS host candidates (w3c/webrtc-pc 3109, reported for all browsers). Add NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription to Info.plist.
- Signaling: the PeerJS cloud still runs and is free (0.peerjs.com/peerjs/id returned 200 in 162 ms today), but it has no SLA, peerjs has had no release since 2025-06, and issue #1350 reports multi-minute WebSocket delays. Fine for a prototype. Recommended for shipping: a Cloudflare Worker plus one Durable Object per room code, WebSocket Hibernation API (ctx.acceptWebSocket; webSocketMessage forwards offer, answer and ICE to the other socket; reject a third socket). About 60 lines. SQLite-backed Durable Objects are on the Workers Free plan (100,000 requests per day; hibernated objects bill no duration). Zero-server alternative: trystero 0.26.0 over public Nostr, BitTorrent or MQTT relays, at the price of depending on third parties.
- STUN and TURN: stun:stun.cloudflare.com:3478 is free and unlimited. STUN alone fails behind symmetric NAT and CGNAT. Cloudflare Realtime TURN costs $0.05 per GB of egress with the first 1,000 GB per month free. The Worker mints short-lived credentials: POST https://rtc.live.cloudflare.com/v1/turn/keys/$TURN_KEY_ID/credentials/generate-ice-servers with Authorization: Bearer $TURN_KEY_API_TOKEN and body {'ttl': 86400} (max 48 h); drop the port 53 URLs for browsers. A relayed 2-player match is well under 50 MB per hour.
Sources: https://developers.cloudflare.com/realtime/turn/generate-credentials/ , https://developers.cloudflare.com/realtime/turn/faq , https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/platform/pricing/ , https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/best-practices/websockets/ , https://github.com/peers/peerjs/issues/1350 , https://github.com/w3c/webrtc-pc/issues/3109 , https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri-docs/issues/3171 , https://caniwebview.com/features/web-feature-webrtc/
